1 شَقَى , inf. n. شَقْىٌ, said of the نَاب [or tush] of a camel, It grew forth: a dial. var. of شَقَأَ. (K in art. شقو [but belonging to the present art.: mentioned in the TA, as not in the K, on the authority of ISd].) ―
-b2- [Freytag states, as on the authority of Abu-l-'Alà, that شَقَى is used for شَقَّ He clave, or split, &c.: ―
-b3- and that Reiske has explained it as signifying He opened the mouth with a wide grinning (“ amplo rictu ” ).]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
